q.t: The place where a river begins is its…
q.e: The source is usually on high ground.

q.t: The place where a river meets the sea is its…
q.e: The mouth is where the river ends.

q.t: A smaller river that joins a bigger one is a…
q.e: Tributaries add their water to the main river.

q.t: The fan of many small channels at a river's mouth is a…
q.e: A river splits into many channels as it drops soil near the sea.

q.t: The Godavari is called…
q.e: It flows through southern India and is the second longest Indian river.

q.t: A giant wall that blocks a river to store water is a…
q.e: A dam stores water in a reservoir behind it.

q.t: A river that flows all year round is…
q.e: Perennial rivers have water even in the dry season.

q.t: Mangrove forests grow where…
q.e: Mangroves survive salty, muddy, waterlogged ground at deltas.

q.t: Which animal is India's national aquatic animal?
q.e: The Ganges river dolphin is blind and finds its way by sound.

q.t: Which programme works to clean the Ganga?
q.e: Namami Gange aims to keep the river healthy for people and wildlife.

q.t: Why does a river get bigger as it flows?
o: Tributaries and rain keep adding water
q.e: Every joining stream adds water and none takes it away.

q.t: Why does a river drop soil at its mouth?
o: The water slows down and can't carry its load
q.e: Slow water can't carry soil, so it settles and builds the delta.

q.t: Why do some rivers keep flowing in the dry season?
o: They are fed by melting snow or groundwater
q.e: A river fed only by rain stops when the rain stops.

q.t: Why were ancient cities built beside rivers?
o: Water is heavy and hard to carry far
q.e: People needed water close by; rivers also gave fertile soil, fish and boat routes.

q.t: Which is a benefit of a dam?
o: Water stored for the dry season
q.e: A dam stores water for irrigation, electricity and the dry months.

q.t: Which is a cost of a dam?
q.e: The reservoir floods land upstream, displacing people and wildlife.

q.t: Sugar dissolved in water can't be seen. Why is this important for safety?
o: Harmful chemicals can be invisible too
q.e: 'It looks clean' is not evidence that water is safe to drink.

q.t: Moving water only knee-deep can…
q.e: That's why we're told not to walk through flood water.

q.t: In 2019, Chennai ran special water trains because…
q.e: Drought left the city with too little water.

q.t: Why does the Ganges dolphin suffer in noisy, polluted water?
o: It is blind and finds its way by sound
It needs clear water to see
q.e: Noise interferes with the sound it uses to navigate.

q.t: How does cutting trees make floods worse?
o: Rain reaches the river all at once instead of slowly
q.e: Same rain, different timing: without trees, the water rushes down together.

q.t: Fertiliser washed into a river forms a 'green blanket'. Why do fish die?
o: Rotting plants use up the oxygen in the water
q.e: Algae grow fast, block sunlight, die and rot — rotting uses up dissolved oxygen.

q.t: Why is building a dam a hard decision?
o: People who gain and people who lose are different
q.e: Benefits go downstream; costs fall upstream on others.

q.t: Which reduces the harm of a dam?
q.e: Planned costs like resettlement, minimum flow and fish ladders reduce harm.

q.t: Fish ladders at dams help…
o: Migrating fish get past the dam
q.e: They give fish a route around the dam wall.

q.t: Why does drought often make people move permanently, but floods usually don't?
o: A drought has no known end date
q.e: Flood water goes down and people rebuild; a drought can go on with nothing to wait for.

q.t: Oil poured in water floats; sugar dissolves. Harmful soapy waste behaves like…
q.e: Many harmful substances dissolve and leave water looking clean.

q.t: Which is NOT a problem caused by floods?
q.e: Flood problems include dirty water, disease, lost crops, broken roads and closed schools.

q.t: A tributary joins a main river rather than the other way round because…
o: The land tilts towards the main river
q.e: Water flows downhill; the land slopes towards the larger river.

q.t: The Coringa forest grows at the Godavari delta. What type of forest is it?
q.e: Mangroves survive where fresh and salty water mix.

q.t: A river carries soil all the way down. Where does most of it settle?
o: Where the water slows near the mouth
q.e: Slow water drops its load — building banks and islands at the mouth.

q.t: A river covered in green algae looks full of life. Why is it actually dying?
o: Too much plant growth uses up oxygen and blocks light
q.e: The harm came from too much of a good thing in the wrong place.

q.t: Which household habit best saves water?
o: Washing cars daily with a hose
q.e: Unnoticed losses like leaks are always bigger than the ones you see.

q.t: Bengaluru flooded in 2022 while Chennai had drought in 2019. What does this teach?
o: We must prepare for both too little and too much water
q.e: Both extremes happen in the same country within a few years.

q.t: A town gets its water from a seasonal river. Its biggest problem would be…
o: No water for months in the dry season
q.e: A seasonal river stops flowing when the rains end.

q.t: Why is the river below a dam often poorer for farmers?
o: Less water and silt reach the land
q.e: The dam holds back both water and the fertile silt.

q.t: Which is the best evidence that water may be unsafe though it looks clear?
o: Sugar dissolves completely and can't be seen
q.e: If sugar can hide in clear water, so can harmful chemicals.

q.t: Dams make electricity using…
q.e: Water falling from the reservoir turns turbines.

q.t: During a flood warning, which is the safest choice?
q.e: Getting higher keeps you away from rising, fast-moving water.

q.t: The Godavari has many tributaries. Rain falling anywhere in its valley…
o: Eventually drains into the same river
q.e: The whole valley collects water into one main channel.
